mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES from t-2w to t-0w signals recovering commuting and weekday foot traffic. That recovery should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks if it continues, because more workers generate more lunch, errand, and after-work purchases.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -59.9 at t-2w to -27.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not remain above its t-2w trough and RETAIL_REC is still lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further improvement in RESIDENTIAL mobility after sustained elevation indicates more time spent near home and weaker willingness to travel for discretionary shopping. If RESIDENTIAL stays above its prior four-week level, RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 15 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained positive in all four weeks and was 13.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 15 and RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT begins recovering from a deep trough, retail access improves with commuting and cross-neighborhood trips. A week-on-week rise in TRANSIT should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks, especially if workplaces also improve.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week after being below -55
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -65.1 at t-2w to -50.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises above the trigger but RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks, or if WORKPLACES weakens at the same time and retail still rises, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A policy tightening regime that suppresses transit and workplaces should spill into lower retail visits. If TRANSIT remains below -50 and WORKPLACES below -30, RETAIL_REC should stay lower over the next four weeks than in the previous four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both transit and workplaces remain substantially below baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: If transit and workplaces remain deeply negative yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM indicates normalization of short local trips and household stock-up behavior. Once grocery mobility improves for two consecutive weeks, retail-and-recreation activity should improve within one week as people re-enter discretionary outing routines.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -24.3 at t-2w to -13.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If grocery mobility rises for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in PARKS after an earlier high signals fading outdoor substitution, which can redirect leisure time back toward malls, restaurants, and entertainment venues. When PARKS falls sharply from its recent peak, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 10 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -24.9 at t-0w after being -38.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS drops by 10 or more points and RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Retail spending recovers when transit and workplaces improve together, because the joint rise captures both access and destination demand. If both series turn upward from their recent lows, RETAIL_REC should be higher four weeks later than in the previous four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve but RETAIL_REC still declines over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If residential time remains elevated while transit stays weak, households are substituting away from discretionary travel. That combination should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 12 while TRANSIT remains below -45
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 13.6 and TRANSIT was -50.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If residential remains above 12 and transit remains below -45 yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
